answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making each new agent identity pay a non-refundable stake and lock it behind a slow proof-of-work challenge before it can earn trust. Every new identity must solve a cipher puzzle whose cost rises with the number of fresh ids, then bond tokens that a bad answer forfeits. Because reputation only accrues on bonded ids, a farmer cloning fake accounts must pay the stake and compute for each, turning a meadow of cheap aliases into one trellis where forgery costs more than honest work.
